subject: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@finpath.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath

Hi Amanda —

First, I'm very sorry for the disruption you experienced this morning. I wanted to share an immediate customer-facing summary of what happened, our mitigations, and the actions we're taking to prevent recurrence. Attached: a one-page timeline and a short SOP for the temporary workaround our SREs executed.

Summary (high level)
- Incident window: 2026-08-27 08:47–10:23 PDT.
- Impact: elevated 5xx errors on text-generation endpoints routed to us by FinPath, causing timeouts for some production requests and degraded throughput.
- Root cause (initial): a cascading resource exhaustion triggered by a memory leak in a third-party dependency during a large batched workload.

Immediate mitigation actions taken
1) Auto-fallback routing enabled for impacted routes to lower-capacity model variants at 08:52 PDT.
2) SREs reclaimed memory and rotated affected inference workers; full worker recycle completed at 09:47 PDT.
3) Temporary rate limits and prioritization policies applied for your production keys until full remediation.

Next steps (what we're doing for FinPath)
- Short-term: we will keep the fallback policy enabled for 72 hours and monitor error rates; we will also share logs for the incident window.
- Medium-term: patch rollout for the dependency causing the leak is scheduled for 2026-08-30 (downtime not required).
- Long-term: add automated leak-detection in our canary pipeline and expand memory quotas for similar batched workloads.

We want to schedule a 30-minute call with your ops team tomorrow morning to walk through the timeline and answer questions. Can you confirm a window between 09:00–11:00 PDT?

Attachments: incident-timeline-20260827.pdf, mitigation-workaround-steps.md

Again, I'm sorry for the disruption. We know FinPath relies on predictable inference performance and we take this seriously.

Respectfully,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Amanda Li <amanda@finpath.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:28:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath

Thanks, Laura. Appreciated — that level of detail is helpful. A couple quick questions for our security and platform teams:

1) Was any customer data exfiltrated or exposed during the incident window?
2) Can you provide request IDs or slices of logs for 09:00–09:30 PDT so our on-call can correlate?

We can do a call tomorrow at 09:30 PDT if that works.

— Amanda
Amanda Li
VP, Platform Engineering
FinPath Analytics
amanda@finpath.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@finpath.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 15:05:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath

Amanda —

Short answers up front: no evidence of data exfiltration; we have preserved the logs and are providing scoped slices. Details below and in the attached timeline.

On data exposure: our investigation (live at 15:00 PDT) shows the failure mode was internal resource exhaustion; requests that returned 5xx did not return payloads beyond normal error messages. We have retained request/response logs for the window and isolated them to a read-only archive; those logs have been hashed and the hashes verified.

Requested artifacts we will share before the call
- Filtered log slices (request IDs and headers) for 08:47–10:23 PDT (redacted to remove any PII per our standard practices).
- Worker-level metrics (memory, CPU) and a per-instance event timeline.
- The SRE incident runbook we executed (mitigation-workaround-steps.md).

We will share a secure Drive folder (read-only) with the above artifacts by 18:00 PDT today. Link will be provided in the meeting invite.

If you have any specific request IDs you want prioritized, reply with those IDs and we'll pull them first.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@finpath.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 18:01:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath

Amanda —

Confirmed: call scheduled for 2026-08-28 at 09:30 PDT (calendar invite sent). The secure Drive folder is here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cFinPath-Incident-2026. It contains: incident-timeline-20260827.pdf, filtered-logs-08-47_to_10-23.zip (redacted), mitigation-workaround-steps.md, and the draft post-incident action tracker (post-incident-action-items.xlsx).

High-level action items we're committing to for FinPath (owner / ETA)
- Patch dependency and complete validation (Engineering / 2026-08-30).
- Add automated leak detection to canary runs (SRE / 2026-09-10).
- Increase memory quotas for batched inference lanes used by FinPath (Product Ops / 2026-09-03).
- Provide an error-rate SLA credit proposal after we complete the post-incident review (Finance & CS / by 2026-09-07).

We'll walk through these items during tomorrow's call and confirm deliverables.

Laura
From: Amanda Li <amanda@finpath.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption briefing and next steps for FinPath

Thanks, Laura and team — confirmed for 09:30. I reviewed the Drive folder and the artifacts look good. We won't need anything else before the call; our on-call will bring a couple of request IDs if we want deeper traces.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear action items.

— Amanda
